intro: The striped skunk (Mephitis mephitis) is the skunk behind essentially every Flovilla call, and it stays active year-round here rather than denning down for a northern-style winter. Two things make this small Indian Springs community skunk-prone: the park's wooded acreage feeds a steady source population onto the surrounding rural lots, and those same lots offer grub-rich lawns to forage and porches, sheds, and crawlspaces to den beneath. Because skunks are one of Georgia's leading rabies carriers, trapping and removal here is a licensed-contractor job, not a DIY one.
extendedBody:
Why Flovilla Sees Steady Skunk Activity

Flovilla is a small rural community pressed up against Indian Springs State Park, and the park's habitat along Big Sandy Creek and McIntosh Lake sustains a continuous striped-skunk population that spills out onto the adjacent rural-residential lots. Once on a property, a skunk wants two things Flovilla yards readily supply: a meal and a den. The meal is usually grubs and soil insects — the source of the cone-shaped overnight digs that pock a lawn — and the den is the open space under a porch, deck, shed, or crawlspace.

The reason to keep your distance is public health. The striped skunk is among Georgia's primary rabies vectors, so a skunk denning against an occupied home is more than a nuisance, and any direct contact with the animal or an active den should be avoided.

The Skunk Under the Porch — and Why Timing Decides the Method

A skunk denned beneath a structure is the standard Flovilla call, and the right response turns on the season:

  • Spring is kit season (roughly February through May). Females raise immobile young under decks, porches, and outbuildings. Trapping out or sealing out the mother in that window leaves the litter to die in the den — an inhumane result and a far worse odor and decomposition problem than the skunk you started with.
  • Outside that window, trapping works; inside it, eviction does. When kits may be present, the family is encouraged out on its own and the den is sealed only once it is confirmed empty.
  • DIY trapping invites a spray. A cornered or trap-stressed skunk discharges, and spray under a porch or in a crawlspace soaks into soil and wood and lingers for weeks; handling and transport also fall under state regulation and carry a rabies-exposure risk.

If a Spray Already Happened

When a dog takes a direct hit or a skunk lets go under the house, the odor saturates fur, soil, insulation, and wood. Enzyme-based deodorizers far outperform the old tomato-juice remedy, which only masks it, and spray inside a crawlspace usually needs professional oxidizing treatment to clear from a confined space. Removing the animal and sealing the den is part of the same job, so the smell does not return with the next skunk.

Keeping Skunks Off the Property

  • Treat for grubs. The nightly cone-shaped lawn digs are a skunk hunting grubs; reducing them removes the main reason it forages your yard.
  • Secure food — latched trash, no overnight pet food, cleaned-up fruit and birdseed.
  • Seal under-structure access with 1/4-inch hardware cloth trenched into the soil and bent outward in an L-footer, so a skunk cannot re-dig its way under the porch, deck, shed, or crawlspace.
  • Clear harborage — woodpiles, brush, and dense growth against the foundation that give a skunk daytime cover. All work follows Georgia DNR Wildlife Resources Division practice.

faqs.q: What does skunk removal cost in Flovilla?
faqs.a: It is set by the season and the sealing. An outside-kit-season trap-and-remove from under one porch is the low end; an eviction during kit season, or a rural Flovilla lot where several structures need their skirting sealed, runs higher. Spray decontamination is a separate add-on. An inspection gives the number.

Beyond the spray, yes in one specific way: the striped skunk is one of Georgia's primary rabies carriers, so a skunk denning against an occupied home is a public-health concern. Keep people and pets away from the animal and the den, and let a licensed contractor handle removal.

faqs.q: A skunk is denning under my Flovilla porch — what now?
faqs.a: Don't try to trap it yourself, and don't seal it in. In spring there are likely immobile kits, so the den is cleared by eviction and only sealed once confirmed empty; outside that window it is trapped and removed, then the access is closed with buried hardware cloth so the next skunk can't re-dig in.

faqs.q: When are skunks most active around Flovilla?
faqs.a: Year-round — Georgia's skunks don't go into deep winter dormancy. Lawn-digging picks up when grubs are near the surface, and den complaints peak in late winter and spring around the February-to-May kit season.

faqs.q: Does tomato juice get rid of skunk smell?
faqs.a: Not really — it mostly masks it. Enzyme-based deodorizers work far better on a sprayed dog, and spray that has soaked into a crawlspace or under a porch usually needs professional oxidizing treatment to clear from the enclosed space.
